items.note: The habit of the readers is to stop on a final moving letter with a sukūn. The report comes from Abū ʿAmr and the Kūfiyyūn that they stopped pointing to the vowel, by rawm or ishmām. The book says nothing is reported about the rest, and that most of the author's teachers prefer pointing for all.

items.note: Ḥamza, from the narration of Khalaf, pauses briefly on a silent letter at the end of a word before a hamza (من آمن, الأرض, الآخرة), and in a single word only on شيء and شيئا. The author reads the same with the pause on the lām of the article and on شيء to Abū al-Ḥasan in both narrations. The book says the rest join the silent letter to the hamza without a pause.
